chunks.text: Financial Sector – Online Loan Processing System Source Requirement Document Synthetic requirement document for testing an evidence-grounded requirement engineering system. 1. System Overview The proposed system is an online loan processing platform for a financial institution. Customers should be able to submit loan applications digitally. The platform will collect customer information, verify identity, assess eligibility, process supporting documents, and route applications for approval or rejection. 2. Business Requirements BR-001: The system shall allow eligible customers to submit loan applications online. BR-002: The system shall reduce manual processing of loan applications.

BR-003: The system shall provide customers with the current status of their loan application. BR-004: The system shall support authorized employees in reviewing and processing loan applications. 3. Functional Requirements FR-001: The system shall allow a customer to create and submit a loan application. FR-002: The system shall collect applicant identity, contact, employment, income, and financial information. FR-003: The system shall allow applicants to upload documents required for loan processing. FR-004: The system shall verify the applicant's identity before the application proceeds to further processing.

FR-005: The system shall perform an eligibility or credit assessment using the available applicant information. FR-006: The system shall route eligible applications to an authorized loan officer for review. FR-007: The system shall record the approval or rejection decision for each completed application. FR-008: The system shall notify the customer when the application status changes. FR-009: The system shall integrate with the institution's existing customer information system. FR-010: The system shall prevent an application from proceeding when mandatory information or documents are missing. 4.

Security and Privacy Requirements SEC-001: Only authenticated users shall be allowed to access their loan applications. SEC-002: Only authorized employees shall be allowed to view or modify customer loan information. SEC-003: Sensitive customer and financial information shall be protected from unauthorized access. SEC-004: The system shall maintain appropriate access controls for customer and employee roles. SEC-005: Communication between the loan platform and external or internal services shall be protected. PRI-001: Customer personal and financial information shall only be used for authorized loan-processing purposes. 5.

Audit and Compliance Requirements AUD-001: The system shall maintain an audit trail of important loan-processing activities. AUD-002: The audit trail shall record significant changes to application status and decisions. AUD-003: Access to sensitive loan information shall be traceable to the responsible user or service. COMP-001: The system shall support applicable financial-institution policies and compliance requirements. COMP-002: Compliance-related requirements shall be reviewed by an authorized compliance or legal representative before final approval. 6.

Performance and Availability Requirements PERF-001: The system should provide timely responses during normal loan application activities. PERF-002: The system should process submitted applications without unnecessary delay. AVL-001: The loan application service should be available during the institution's defined service hours. AVL-002: Failures in external verification or credit-assessment services shall be handled without losing the customer's application data. 7. Integration and Legacy Constraints INT-001: The system shall integrate with the existing customer information system. INT-002: The system shall integrate with an identity-verification service.

INT-003: The system shall integrate with an approved credit-assessment or scoring service where required. CON-001: Existing customer data and interfaces may impose constraints on the design of the new platform. 8. Open Issues and Assumptions The exact loan eligibility rules have not yet been finalized. The exact response-time targets have not yet been defined. The specific external identity-verification provider has not yet been selected. The applicable regulatory requirements depend on the institution's jurisdiction and must be verified by authorized personnel. The final loan approval authority and escalation rules require confirmation from the business and compliance teams. 9.

Purpose of This Document This synthetic document is intended to provide source material for testing an AI-based requirement engineering workflow. The system should use the information in this document as evidence when generating additional structured requirements for a specified loan-processing functionality. Unsupported assumptions should be identified rather than presented as established facts.

factors.name: Requirement stability
factors.rationale: Draft or unapproved requirements indicate that stability has not yet been demonstrated.

factors.name: Requirement clarity
factors.rationale: Measured from the presence of concrete, non-placeholder acceptance criteria.

factors.name: Risk
factors.rationale: Derived from stated high risk and security, privacy, regulatory, or audit classifications.

factors.name: Complexity
factors.rationale: Integration and data-management requirements increase coordination and technical complexity.

factors.name: Need for early prototype
factors.rationale: Unclear requirements or integration complexity make early learning and validation valuable.

factors.name: Time constraints
factors.rationale: No schedule or deadline evidence is available in the generated requirements; confirm this with the project sponsor.

factors.name: Customer involvement
factors.rationale: Derived only from business, stakeholder, or usability requirements; otherwise this must be confirmed.

factors.name: Frequency of changes
factors.rationale: Requirement documents do not establish the expected change rate; confirm with product and business stakeholders.

factors.name: Need for iterative development
factors.rationale: Unapproved or unclear requirements benefit from repeated review and validation cycles.

factors.name: Need for risk analysis
factors.rationale: Security/compliance concerns or complex integration warrant explicit risk analysis.

options.name: Spiral
options.suitability: Best when risk analysis, prototypes, and repeated risk-reduction cycles are central.

options.name: Prototyping
options.suitability: Best for validating uncertain user needs, workflows, and interfaces before committing to a full build.

options.name: Agile
options.suitability: Best for frequent feedback and evolving requirements, with planned governance for high-risk work.

options.name: Incremental
options.suitability: Best when value can be divided into validated, independently testable increments.

options.name: V-Shape
options.suitability: Best when each specification stage needs a linked verification and validation activity.

options.name: RAD
options.suitability: Best for time-boxed delivery with available users and modular, lower-risk scope.

options.name: Waterfall
options.suitability: Best when requirements are stable, fully specified, and changes are controlled.

sdlc.justification: Spiral has the highest transparent score because requirement stability is needs validation, requirement clarity is low, risk is high, complexity is high, need for early prototype is likely. Factors marked 'Not evidenced' are deliberately neutral and require stakeholder confirmation before the SDLC is approved.
